title: Ἵππος καὶ ἱπποκόμος
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 140. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Κριθὴν τὴν τοῦ ἵππου ὁ ἱπποκόμος κλέπτων καὶ πωλῶν τὸν ἵππον ἔτριβεν, ἐκτένιζεν πᾶσαν ἡμέραν.
sentences.tr: Krithēn tēn tou hippou ho hippokomos kleptōn kai pōlōn ton hippon etriben, ektenizen pasan hēmeran.
sentences.l: The groom, stealing and selling the horse's barley, rubbed the horse down and combed him out all day long.
sentences.n: κριθή, barley, is the horse's feed: what the groom is selling is the animal's own ration. ἔτριβεν, ἐκτένιζεν stand side by side with no connective at all, a bare pairing that hurries the line; both are customary imperfects — this was his daily practice. πᾶσαν ἡμέραν is an accusative of extent of time.

sentences.t: Ἔφη δὲ ὁ ἵππος· « Εἰ θέλεις ἀληθῶς καλὸν εἶναί με, τὴν κριθὴν τὴν τρέφουσάν με μὴ πώλει. »
sentences.tr: Ephē de ho hippos· « Ei theleis alēthōs kalon einai me, tēn krithēn tēn trephousan me mē pōlei. »
sentences.l: And the horse said: « If you truly wish me to be handsome, do not sell the barley that feeds me. »
sentences.n: θέλω takes an infinitive with its own accusative subject, εἶναί με, "for me to be". καλός of a horse is "in fine condition, good to look at" — the whole object of a groom's work, which is the joke. μὴ πώλει is a present imperative with μή: not "do not sell it once" but "stop selling it", forbidding a practice already under way.

sentences.t: Ὅτι οἱ πλεονέκται τοῖς πιθανοῖς λόγοις καὶ ταῖς κολακείαις τοὺς πένητας δελεάζοντες ἀποστεροῦσιν αὐτοὺς καὶ τῆς ἀναγκαίας χρείας.
sentences.tr: Hoti hoi pleonektai tois pithanois logois kai tais kolakeiais tous penētas deleazontes aposterousin autous kai tēs anankaias chreias.
sentences.l: That the greedy, baiting the poor with plausible words and with flatteries, rob them even of their necessary sustenance.
sentences.i: The story shows that the greedy bait the poor with plausible words and with flattery, and rob them even of what they cannot do without.
sentences.n: A moral in the bare Ὅτι form: the introducing verb is unexpressed in the Greek, which begins simply "That…", and is supplied in the idiomatic line. πιθανός is "persuasive, plausible" — words built to convince, with no claim to be true. δελεάζω is to put bait on a hook. ἀποστερέω takes the accusative of the person and the genitive of the thing taken from him; καί before τῆς ἀναγκαίας χρείας is "even".
